public_rationale: The evidence supports persistent weaknesses in the tested models across all four areas. October studies give particularly relevant evidence for mathematical and psychological reasoning. However, the causal and physical studies cover earlier models and do not adequately establish the December 6 state of the whole field. Strong causal results and large gains from targeted social-reasoning prompts also deserve weight. None establishes that an entire area was solved, but the retrieved record is insufficient to support Marcus's full 'not one' statement without extrapolating beyond the tested models.
limitations: The assessment concerns December 2024 capabilities, not subsequent progress.
Benchmark failures establish limits under particular tasks and methods; they do not prove that LLMs lack reasoning altogether.
The physical evaluation combines perception with reasoning and therefore does not isolate reasoning failures.

our_interpretation: Read 'robustly solved' as dependable performance across varied, unfamiliar problems and relevant variations within an area. This does not require perfect performance.
Read psychological reasoning as reasoning about people's beliefs, knowledge, intentions and behavior.

The observation concerns LLM capabilities on 6 December 2024. Use the current calendar year through the post as the public evaluation window because model evaluations have no fixed reporting cycle. Earlier evaluations within that window require caution when applied to the December state of the field.

Success on selected examples or a narrow benchmark does not establish that an entire reasoning area was solved. Conversely, failures by older or weaker models do not establish that every contemporary model retained those weaknesses.
criteria.support_condition: Broad evaluations of capable LLMs available by the post establish substantial, reproducible failures on unfamiliar problems or relevant variations in each of the four areas, with sufficient model coverage to support the December 2024 observation.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evaluations establish dependable performance across varied novel problems and relevant variations throughout at least one named area in an LLM available by the post.

evidence.explanation: CaLM evaluates 28 models across 92 causal targets and reports worsening performance as causal tasks become more complex. This supports persistent causal weaknesses in the tested population, but does not establish the capabilities of every model available in December.

evidence.excerpt: struggle with answering these physical questions.
evidence.explanation: ContPhy finds failures by GPT-4V and Gemini on physical properties and dynamics, particularly cloth and fluids, while also recording successes on some rope and ball tasks. The models receive sampled video frames, so perception and the input format may contribute to failures; these are also early-2024 model evaluations.

evidence.locator: Section 5.1, Judgment of behavior; prompting controls in section 5.3
evidence.explanation: SimpleToM finds a gap between identifying mental states and applying them: o1-preview reaches 59.5% on behavior judgments despite stronger performance on the preceding tasks. Material counterevidence within the same study is that targeted reminders and reasoning prompts produce high scores, including a 97.1% average for Claude-3.5-Sonnet under the combined intervention.

evidence.locator: Figure 8(a) caption; section 4.4 and appendix A.5
evidence.explanation: Adding irrelevant information to mathematical word problems produces substantial failures, including for o1-preview. The study also acknowledges strong o1 performance on other variants; these results establish a robustness weakness rather than an absence of mathematical ability.

This revised study reports strong causal-task performance and tests on datasets created after model training cutoffs, making it material counterevidence to an overly dismissive reading. It also reports unpredictable errors and prompt sensitivity, so it does not establish that causal reasoning as a whole was robustly solved.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Version-specific evaluations of leading models available by 6 December 2024, especially in causal and physical reasoning, testing varied unfamiliar problems and effective prompting. Persistent substantial failures across all four areas would support the claim; broad reliable performance across any one area would contradict it.
